title: Oil for cold butter that's rubbed in

evidence.basis: B4. OD-7 (owner commission 2026-10-08, ENGINEERING only; not culinary validation, not released guidance). Evidence: private/research/substitution-knowledge (2026-10-07). Milk Street SRC-BO-41#a (oil a poor substitute where cold butter is cut in: sodden dough); Utah State SRC-BO-34#a; Purdue SRC-BO-40#g; New Mexico State SRC-BO-37#c; KA SRC-BO-14#b (warm fat: dense, leaden biscuits). Recipes written for oil are not a substitution case.

text: Oil can't stand in for the cold butter rubbed into this dough: the butter has to stay in solid pieces that melt in the oven, and liquid oil soaks into the flour instead, giving a sodden, dense dough.
scopeNote: This is about oil in place of cold butter that's rubbed in; recipes written for oil are different. It isn't a verdict on other replacements.
answer: can't be rubbed in as solid pieces
